tier_reason: Independent third-party suite (andre-wojtowicz/blas-benchmarks, not by the ATLAS authors) with public harness code (slave-cmds.sh installs each library and LD_PRELOADs it under Rscript; benchmark-urbanek.R is R-benchmark-25, mean of 10 runs) and stated CPU models; the chart images show ATLAS (st) at 1.50 s vs Netlib 11.41 s (x7.6) and 0.747 s vs 5.466 s (x7.3) on the Xeon E3-1275 v5 and 1.58 s vs 9.45 s (x6.0) on the Xeon E5-1620 v4. Not A because compiler and flags are never stated (ATLAS st and Netlib are Debian binary packages; ATLAS mt is built with ATLAS's own configure defaults on an unstated gcc).

corrections.compiler_and_flags: Not stated. ATLAS (st) 3.10.2 and Netlib (blas 1.2.20110419, lapack 3.5.0) are Debian Jessie binary packages (libatlas3-base, libblas3/liblapack3) installed from a snapshot.debian.org 20160411 jessie-backports mirror, so the ATLAS (st) library was not auto-tuned on the test host; ATLAS (mt) 3.11.38 was built from source with '../configure --shared --with-netlib-lapack-tarfile=lapack-3.6.0.tgz' (Debian build-essential gcc/gfortran, version not stated) after patching config.c (thrchk=0) and archinfo_x86.c (adds CPU model 0x5E); CPU governor set to performance.
corrections.claimed_speedup: Single-threaded ATLAS 3.10.2 (Debian package) vs Netlib reference BLAS, R-benchmark-25 mean of 10 runs (chart bar labels and 'Performance gain' column in the README images): Xeon E3-1275 v5 2800x2800 cross-product 1.50 s vs 11.41 s (x7.6), 2000x2000 linear regression 0.747 s vs 5.466 s (x7.3); Xeon E5-1620 v4 cross-product 1.58 s vs 9.45 s (x6.0). Multi-threaded ATLAS dev branch 3.11.38 reaches 0.14 s (x79.3) on the E3-1275 v5 cross-product. Against in-list baselines the multi-threaded ATLAS build roughly ties: i7-4790K cross-product ATLAS (mt) 0.13 s vs OpenBLAS 0.14 s, BLIS 0.15 s, MKL 0.17 s; i5-3570 OpenBLAS 0.27 s vs ATLAS (mt) 0.28 s, MKL 0.28 s, BLIS 0.28 s.
corrections.stars_or_usage: 192 stars, 37 forks (GitHub mirror); last SourceForge stable release 3.10.3 dated 2016-07-28, last developer release 3.11.41 dated 2018-10-05; shipped as a Debian package
corrections.caveats: The headline win is over the unoptimised Netlib reference BLAS, which is not one of the category's listed baselines (OpenBLAS, MKL, Eigen, BLIS). In the same charts single-threaded ATLAS is slower than OpenBLAS 0.2.12 (0.49 s vs 1.50 s on the E3-1275 v5 cross-product), GotoBLAS2 (0.92 s) and Intel MKL (0.14 s), but those, BLIS and ATLAS (mt) are multi-threaded builds in this suite, so the single-threaded comparison is not like-for-like (single-threaded ATLAS does beat the multi-threaded BLIS dev build on the E3-1275 v5: 1.50 s vs 1.75 s). The multi-threaded ATLAS 3.11.38 lead over OpenBLAS on the E3-1275 v5 (0.14 s vs 0.49 s) and E5-1620 v4 (0.15 s vs 0.53 s) is probably not a fair in-list win: OpenBLAS was a 2014 Debian 0.2.12 package older than both CPUs, while the ATLAS (mt) build was patched to recognise CPU model 0x5E; on the older i7-4790K and i5-3570 hosts ATLAS (mt), OpenBLAS, BLIS and MKL are within about 10% of each other. Numbers are read from bar-chart images embedded in the README (the page has no text tables; bars are means of 10 runs); compiler and flags are not stated; ATLAS (st) is the Debian package, so ATLAS's install-time tuning was not run on the host; 2016-era hardware and library versions; the suite is a small third-party repo (33 stars, Zenodo DOI) rather than a famous shootout. ATLAS's own timing pages (math-atlas.sourceforge.net/timing/) give DGEMM percent-of-peak (e.g. 89% on a 2.4 GHz Core2) without any baseline. The ATLAS papers (Whaley and Dongarra) were not reachable here. Project inactive since 2019-06-11; the last stable release is 3.10.3 (2016-07-28) and the last developer release 3.11.41 (2018-10-05).

notes: Numbers match the README chart images exactly; ATLAS is a genuine, widely shipped auto-tuned BLAS but its only clear win is over Netlib reference BLAS (baseline_in_list corrected to false). Shortcomings to record: baseline off-list (Netlib reference); single-threaded ATLAS slower than multi-threaded OpenBLAS/MKL/GotoBLAS2 in the same charts; multi-threaded ATLAS only ties OpenBLAS/MKL/BLIS on CPUs the 2014 OpenBLAS 0.2.12 package supports; compiler and flags unstated; abandoned since 2019. The record's '3.10.3 dated 2018-10-05' was the developer release 3.11.41; stable 3.10.3 is 2016-07-28.
